thread:
Sasha M.: kicking off a quick internal run to help set sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst handling. want a short repro + playbook we can hand to support. running chat-like payloads now

Matt L.: nice — single-key or multi-tenant? what durations and token sizes?

Sasha M.: single api key first. simulating chat sessions, 60-200 token replies, 1k concurrent sockets. plan: sweep rps/rpm and burst bucket sizes. will paste commands + early results.

Sasha M.: command i used:
```
loadlab run --scenario=chat --keys=1 --concurrency=1000 --rps=300 --duration=5m --burst=600
```

Sasha M.: early observations: sustained 300 RPM (5 rps) per key triggers 429s after ~30s. token-bucket refill is the limiter not GPU throughput for this profile. queuing raised p95 latency to ~700ms before errors.

Infra-bot: [test-run-1739991111] finished — duration=5m, peak_rps=18, avg_latency=420ms, 429_count=120, artifacts=/ci/artifacts/1739991111

Jess K.: 429 spike looks like the burst window exhausted. did you try increasing the bucket capacity vs refill rate?

Sasha M.: increased bucket to 1200 in a follow-up — that let traffic absorb a ~90s warm burst but didn't change sustainable throughput because refill rate unchanged. takeaway: defaults need both a safe steady-rate and a modest burst allowance.

Oliver P.: for support docs we should include client retry guidance: exponential backoff with full jitter, max 3 retries for idempotent calls, and a circuit-breaker for repeated 429s.

Matt L.: + monitoring alerts: trigger if 429 or 5xx > 1% over 10m for any key, and alert if per-key burst usage > 70% for 5m. log examples so support can triage fast.

Jess K.: playbook sketch for support: 1) ask customer for exact timing + api-key, 2) run internal rate profile against their key (short smoke), 3) if 429 > 5% escalate to SRE with artifacts, 4) suggest client backoff and lowering RPS.

Sasha M.: proposed default numbers for hosted-tier (draft): steady_rate = 300 RPM (5 RPS), burst_capacity = 600 tokens, burst_window_seconds ~ 60-120. dedicated-tier: steady_rate = 900 RPM, burst_capacity = 2400. note: embeddings and long-response workloads should have lower RPS recommendations.

Support Liaison: tagging @support-team — we'll fold this into triage docs and KB. can we get a short repro snippet support can paste?

Sasha M.: yep — will add the exact loadlab command + link to artifacts and a quick checklist (what to ask customers, what to run internally, when to escalate).

Matt L.: one more: add a small multi-key abuse test (many keys low rps) — that catches distributed token-bucket exhaustion patterns.

Sasha M.: agreed. action items: (a) update playbook with commands and thresholds, (b) add per-key burst metrics to console, (c) add example client retry snippet, (d) schedule a 30m run with multi-key sweep.

Oliver P.: fine by me. leaving a note to support: "if customer reports latency + 429s, test with single-key smoke at 5 rps for 5m and attach infra artifacts before escalation." :thumbsup:

Support Liaison: will incorporate and ping when KB entry is live. thanks everyone.
